articles.title_zh: Susan Smith denied parole again 32 years after drowning her two sons
facts_zh:
Susan Smith denied parole again 32 years after drowning her two sons
- Published
A South Carolina woman who admitted to drowning her two sons 32 years ago has been denied parole for a second time.
Susan Smith, 55, was convicted of killing her boys by strapping them into their car seats and rolling her vehicle into a lake in 1994.
"I got to my lowest when I let that car go into that lake," Smith said during a hearing on Thursday with the state board that decides whether to release those in prison on parole.

articles.title_original: Venezuela signs military deal with US less than a year after Maduro's removal
articles.title_zh: Venezuela signs military deal with US less than a year after Maduro's removal
facts_zh:
Venezuela signs military deal with US less than a year after Maduro's removal
- Published
The United States and Venezuela have re-established military ties less than a year after US forces seized the then-leader of the South American country, Nicolás Maduro, in a raid on the capital, Caracas.
The interim government led by Delcy Rodríguez, Maduro's former vice-president, signed a military co-operation agreement with US Secretary of Defence Pete Hegseth on Wednesday.
Few details about the deal have been released so far but Hegseth said that Venezuela had "gone from our most aggressive regional threat to a compliant security partner" in less than 12 months.

all_titles.en: Venezuela signs military deal with US less than a year after Maduro's removal

articles.title_original: US consortium wins huge Kenya mining deal, beating Chinese rivals
articles.title_zh: US consortium wins huge Kenya mining deal, beating Chinese rivals
facts_zh:
US consortium wins huge Kenya mining deal, beating Chinese rivals
- Published
A US-led consortium, Frontier Minerals, has won the tender to develop Kenya's Mrima Hill mining project, beating seven bidders, including companies from China and Australia.
The site is estimated to hold deposits of critical minerals worth more than $60bn (£45bn), including niobium, used in electric vehicles, aerospace and defence technology.
Frontier Minerals says its proposal aims to keep more of the economic benefits in Kenya through "processing and refining of minerals in-country".

all_titles.en: US consortium wins huge Kenya mining deal, beating Chinese rivals

facts_zh:
Florida pastor found guilty over role in assassination of Haitian president
- Published
A Florida pastor has been found guilty of a number of charges relating to the assassination of the Haitian President Jovenel Moïse.
Christian Emmanuel Sanon, a dual US-Haitian national, was convicted of all eight charges against him, including conspiracy to kill or kidnap a person.
He faces a potential sentence of life in prison.

articles.title_original: Race to replant five South African baobabs after export blocked
articles.title_zh: Race to replant five South African baobabs after export blocked
facts_zh: The trees, intended for an unnamed buyer in Georgia, were reportedly dug up without the necessary permits Environmentalists in South Africa are racing to replant five centuries-old baobabs after the 20-tonne trees were dug up by an exporter, who tried to ship them thousands of miles to Georgia.
The baobabs arrived at a reserve in Timbavati, in north-eastern South Africa, on Wednesday, where they will be replanted and supported by cables to help them recover.
The trees had been stranded at a warehouse in Durban since July, when they were intercepted by authorities who said they had been moved without the necessary permissions.

all_titles.en: Race to replant five South African baobabs after export blocked

articles.title_zh: Survivors of Uganda's deadly landslide seek justice at the UN
facts_zh:
Survivors of Uganda's deadly landslide seek justice at the UN
- Published
Survivors of a 2019 landslide in eastern Uganda that killed more than 50 people have taken their fight for relocation and compensation to the United Nations.
The 48 complainants accuse the government of violating Uganda's constitution by failing to put effective disaster management measures in Bududa, a mountainous district prone to landslides.
Their case comes as heavy rains raise the risk of further landslides.
